messages:
Ben G.: hey, hit a weird 403 in the console after we transferred project 'aurora' into our new org. CLI tokens still work for API calls but the web console errors when i click Projects > aurora -> Settings -> Billing. getting '403 Permission denied' page. Can you help?

Aisha (Support): thanks for the ping — sorry about the blocker. quick q: did you move the project using the org-transfer flow or did you invite the project owner into the new org? also can you paste the full error text or screenshot?

Ben G.: moved via org-transfer UI yesterday evening. Screenshot: https://files.redwood.test/s/beng-403-snap.png (private link). Error says: '403 Forbidden: user lacks permission to view project resources'. CLI returns 200 for /v1/projects/aurora with my personal API key (same account). In console i see my name in the member list but under Effective roles it shows 'no direct role — inherited deny: billing'.

Aisha (Support): good detail — that 'inherited deny' hint is usually the clue. can you run this in console (Admin view) or ask an org-admin to check: Admin > Organization > Memberships > select your user > View effective roles. any deny entries?

Ben G.: yes that's what i pasted above. shows 'inherited deny: project.billing:deny' coming from parent org group 'finance-readonly'. we switched SSO groups during the transfer (Okta SCIM sync).

Sam (SRE): fwiw, we've seen SCIM group attribute renames cause group rebind where old group gets recreated and the new one doesn't carry the allow role. when SCIM creates a new group with same name but new id, role bindings may orphan.

Jules (IAM): tagging in — likely root cause: group-level deny from parent org that was applied during the group sync. two mitigations: 1) remove the deny at the parent org (if policy allows) or 2) add an explicit allow at the project level for your user or the new group. prefer (2) as quick workaround.

Aisha (Support): Ben, can you try this quick workaround (requires org-admin or IAM team): Admin CLI -> run
```
# grant explicit project developer role to your user
redwoodctl auth grant --project aurora --member "ben@example.com" --role project.developer
```
That should override inherited deny for console actions. If you can't run it, we can propose it to the customer's org-admin.

Ben G.: i am not an org-admin, so can't run. can support or IAM do it for us? also worried about permissions scope and audit.

Aisha (Support): we can't change customer orgs directly. we can create a step-by-step for your org-admin and review the audit impact. Also can provide a temporary 'support suggestion' to test: ask org-admin to add you explicitly as project.admin for aurora then try console.

Ben G.: ok i asked our org-admin (Claire) and she's available. Claire did: Admin -> Projects -> aurora -> Members -> Add member -> ben@example.com -> Role: Project Viewer. still 403 on billing page.

Sam (SRE): Project Viewer won't allow billing. need Project Developer or Project Billing role — viewer is read-only over most project resources but billing pages require billing privilege. Claire needs to add project.billing or Project Owner/Developer.

Claire (via Ben): i changed you to Project Billing and you still saw 403. i also removed you then re-added you, still 403.

Jules (IAM): okay that's consistent with an inherited deny taking precedence. In our policy precedence model, explicit allow at the same scope normally wins unless there's an explicit deny from a parent policy flagged 'inherit with deny precedence'. We need to inspect the parent group's policy. Claire can check Admin -> Organization -> Groups -> finance-readonly -> Policies -> Check for 'deny' entries.

Ben G.: parent org group shows a policy 'restrict-billing-access: deny project.billing' applied at org root, created 2026-01-09 during a security baseline change. i guess the org-transfer bumped me into that group?

Aisha (Support): thanks — that lines up. two paths: 1) remove that deny entry (needs security approval) OR 2) create an exception policy for the aurora project to allow billing for members X. recommended: create an org-level exception scoped to a single project to keep baseline.

Sam (SRE): for the exception, Claire (org-admin) can create a policy like:
```
# org console steps
Admin -> Organization -> Policies -> New Policy
Name: allow-billing-aurora-exception
Scope: Project aurora
Effect: Allow project.billing
Targets: users: ben@example.com OR group: aurora-owners
```
That should be evaluated after the deny and produce effective allow for the project scope.

Ben G.: Claire tried adding an exception but UI said 'conflicting policy' on save. error message: 'Policy conflict with inherited deny; contact IAM team'.

Jules (IAM): if the system flags it as conflict we need IAM to relax enforcement or manually create a policy exception via backend. Claire, can you open a support ticket with exact policy ids? include the parent policy id and the exception draft. we'll coordinate with security to approve.

Aisha (Support): i've opened internal escalation to IAM + security with relevant logs and the policy ids pulled from the UI. Reference: INC-2026-00412. attaching console logs.

deploy-bot: incident INC-2026-00412 updated by Aisha (Support): Assigned to IAM team. SLA: 4h.

Jules (IAM): quick note on repro and safe action: do NOT delete the parent deny until security reviews. We can create a project-scoped exception in the backend once we have approval. Timeline: we can have a safe exception in ~2-4 hours after approvals.

Ben G.: thanks — do we expect any service interruption for aurora during this?

Sam (SRE): no service interruption. it's purely auth decision. console access will be restored for permitted actions once exception is in place.

Aisha (Support): next steps for Claire/Org Admin: 1) wait for IAM approval (we've started it) 2) once approved, IAM will apply backend exception 3) Claire should re-login to console (force logout) and clear cookies to refresh effective roles 4) confirm Billing page loads. We'll keep you posted in this thread.

Ben G.: appreciated. keep me posted. :thumbsup:

Aisha (Support): assigning follow-up to Jules. Jules, please update INC-2026-00412 when exception is applied. closing loop here after IAM confirmation. :white_check_mark:

Jules (IAM): will do. updating timeline on ticket.

Ben G.: confirmed after 2.5h — Claire says IAM put the exception in place and i can access billing now. thank you all.

Aisha (Support): great to hear — marking this thread resolved. if anything else crops up reopen and we'll pick it back up. :party:
